subject: Reserved GPU queue stability / temporary SLA variance request
messages:
From: Samuel Teo <samuel@aegiscloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: AegisCloud Procurement <procure@aegiscloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production queue spikes after reserved GPU migration — requesting short-term exception/credits

Hi Karthik / Lauren,

Quick note from our ops team after last week's migration to the reserved GPU pool: during the nightly batch window (approx 02:00-04:00 UTC) we've been seeing intermittent queueing spikes that push tail latency to ~2.0-2.4s for a subset of high-length requests. Overall throughput looks fine, but those tail events are causing timeouts in a downstream transformer stage and three retries at our side.

We understand some variability is expected during steady-state balancing, but this is a repeatable pattern tied to the nightly jobs. Two asks from our side: 1) can Redwood provision a temporary buffer / smoothing policy for that nightly window (e.g., +10% burst or short-term higher concurrency) while our batch cadence is adjusted; and 2) can we get guidance on how this will map to our committed throughput SLA (we're tracking potential business impact and may request a short-term credit if incidents continue).

I'll attach a small packet of timestamps and a short trace map in the follow-up e-mail (ops will send logs). We prefer a quick call to align (30m) if you're available — Samuel and our procurement lead can join.

Thanks,
Samuel Teo
Head of Platform Reliability, AegisCloud
Samuel Teo

[Attachment: — will send logs.zip in next reply]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Samuel Teo <samuel@aegiscloud.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production queue spikes after reserved GPU migration — requesting short-term exception/credits

Sam — thanks for the heads up and the clear summary. Sorry you're seeing that behavior post-migration. We take nightly batch regressions seriously.

A few quick asks so my infra team can triage immediately:
- Can you confirm the p50/p95/p99 numbers around the spike times (a sample is fine)?
- Please send the logs with the exact UTC timestamps for the 02:00-04:00 window (trace IDs help).
- Do you have a sample prompt length distribution for the requests that experienced the spikes?

Operationally, two immediate options we can offer while we investigate:
1) Enable a temporary queue-smoothing policy scoped to your reserved pool for the nightly window (adds short-lived burst capacity and prefers in-flight sessions for 30 days).
2) Flip a non-invasive routing rule to temporarily route long-sequence work to a slightly higher-throughput variant (same model family) that has lower tail variance.

If you want the buffer, we'll need a formal exception request so contracts can document the window and duration. Ben (cc'd) can help on the contractual/credits side.

If you can send the logs now, I'll push the engineering task immediately and propose a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Samuel Teo <samuel@aegiscloud.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: AegisCloud Procurement <procure@aegiscloud.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production queue spikes after reserved GPU migration — requesting short-term exception/credits

Thanks Karthik — attaching the packet now.

Summary from our ops/observability export (attached aegis_cloud_request_logs_20261115.zip):
- Window: 2026-11-15 02:00:00 - 2026-11-15 04:00:00 UTC
- p50: 180ms, p95: 560ms, p99: 2.38s (spikes aligned with batch job kickoff at 02:17 UTC)
- Affected traffic: ~8% of requests (long sequences, mean token length ~1.8x our normal)
- Internal Incident ID: AEG-OPS-2026-11-15-22

We're open to either of the operational mitigations you suggested. From procurement's side, we want to document an SLA variance (temporary window + credit if windows reoccur after mitigation) rather than a long-term contract amendment. If Redwood can agree to a 30-day buffer with monitoring and a one-time credit if a second similar incident occurs, procurement will expedite the paperwork.

Can we do a 30m call tomorrow 10:00 PST to walk the logs and agree next steps? Also attaching a short runbook snippet describing our batch cadence.

Best,
Samuel
[Attachments: aegis_cloud_request_logs_20261115.zip, aegis_batch_runbook_snippet.txt]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production queue spikes after reserved GPU migration — requesting short-term exception/credits

Looping you both in with the logs attached. Quick internal note / proposed plan before we answer formally to AegisCloud:

1) Engineering: Enable queue-smoothing policy scoped to their reserved pool for the nightly window (02:00-04:00 UTC) — this is a non-invasive, short-term burst that preserves latency SLOs for long sequences. Target: enable within 4 business hours and monitor for 72h.

2) Model routing: Prepare an opt-in routing rule to send long-sequence requests to the higher-throughput variant (low-risk, no model change). This buys us time while they tune batch cadence.

3) Contracts/Finance: Offer a documented 30-day exception period ("nightly buffer") with a conditional one-time credit if a second incident of the same class occurs within those 30 days. Ben — can you draft a short amendment (we already have a template) and confirm the credit range we can commit to? I've attached a working draft SLA amendment (sla_amendment_draft_v1.pdf) for review.

4) Customer call: I'll take the 10:00 PST slot tomorrow for a 30m alignment with Samuel and procurement.

If that aligns, I'll reply to Samuel with the operational next steps and include the draft amendment, then loop Contracts for signature.

Thanks — karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
